messages.note: RFC 7617 — the secret is compared in constant time, never logged

messages.label: 200 { access_token, expires_in, token_type, scope }
messages.note: no refresh_token — §4.4.3: there is no person whose absence it would cover

200 data
messages.note: sub = client_id: the token stands for the client itself, not for a person

cards.title: Why there is no refresh token
items: A refresh token stands in for a resource owner who has walked away
Here the subject is the client, and it already holds what mints tokens
When the access token expires it simply asks again with its secret

cards.title: What Basic proves
items: Only a confidential client has a secret to present
A public client sending one is rejected, not quietly accepted
The client must also be registered for client_credentials

cards.title: Scope
items: Omitting scope grants everything in the client's allowedScopes
Supplying it can only narrow that set, never widen it
Anything outside fails with invalid_scope before a token exists
